restoration_note: Teaching 62 narrates the Lord-as-Divine-Human clothing himself in the elements of the natural and standing firm against the first Enmity (the self asserting itself). The strong loves (lions) are given as a garment to the archons of death, who swallow them; what they swallow then bursts back out of their mouths as a river — the river of Judgment, the self's own outpouring read as its sentence. Restoration is well-anchored at clause boundaries (ϩⲙ̄, ⲁⲩⲱ, ⲁⲃⲁⲗ, ⲡⲕⲁϩ, ⲁϩⲣ̄ⲫⲟⲣⲉ paralleling the chapter title) and in formulaic parallels (the 'first Enmity' formula from §3761 governs §3783; ϣⲟ 'thousand' is fixed by §3793). The middle of the passage (§§3770-3782) is too fragmentary for principled fills and is left unrestorable. The summing exclamation at §3797-3799 is restored on the strength of its parallel with §3796.

coptic_restorations.basis: Standard temporal preposition ϩⲙ̄ ⲡⲥⲏⲩ 'in the time'; editor's reading is grammatically required.
Completes ⲁⲣⲉⲧϥ̄ 'his feet' (suffix on ⲣⲉⲧⲉ) within the idiom ⲧⲱⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧ⸗ 'stand firm on one's feet'.
Completes ⲁⲩⲱ 'and'; standard conjunction continuing the description of the contest.
Completes ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'forth' from the directional verb ⲥⲱⲣ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'spread forth' in §3764.
Completes ⲫⲃⲥⲱ = ϩⲃⲥⲱ 'garment' in Lycopolitan orthography (lexicon: ⲍⲃⲥⲱ).
Editor's restoration: perfect ⲁ + indefinite plural 'some/many lions' as subject of ⲱⲟⲩⲟ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ; the modifier ⲉⲛⲁⲱⲱⲟⲩ 'which are many' agrees with this plural subject.

7 chars; comparative 'like a river' fits the immediately preceding image of pouring forth from the garment, which then becomes the river-from-the-mouth-of-archons motif. Standard ⲛ̄ⲑⲉ ⲛ̄ⲟⲩ- 'like a' formula.
11 chars with no traces; could be a verb of establishing or a relative clause introducing the lions/river as 'bearers of destruction'. No principled fill.
Editor's reading: ⲁϥ-ϯ 'he gave' before object ⲛⲉⲕⲉ 'others'; parallels the giving-pattern of §3765-3766.
Relative imperfect 2pl ⲉⲧⲉⲧⲛ̄ⲛⲉⲩ 'that you saw' completes the standard form before ⲛⲛⲉⲩ.
3sg masc suffix ϩ on directional ⲁⲣⲁ⸗, giving ⲁⲣⲁϥ 'to it/him' (the river).
9 chars with partial 'ⲉ . ⲉ'; not enough constraint to determine the verb-form introducing 'they were filled together'. Could be circumstantial or relative, but no principled fill.

3 chars closing in -ⲙ before ·; ⲕⲁⲩⲙⲁ (Greek καῦμα 'burning heat') fits the immediate context of 'their dryness was without downpours' — seasons of burning heat with no rain. Lexicon: drought as withholding of influx.
Initial ⲙ of ⲙⲟⲩⲛ̄ϩⲱⲟⲩ 'downpour' (lexicon: rain as influx descending into the natural).
8 chars with no traces; the noun governing 'their days of being' is unrecoverable.
Genitive completing ⲙ̄ⲡⲓ̈ⲉⲣⲟ 'of that river', linking back to ⲧⲟⲁⲧ 'branch' from §3779.
1 char at line break; insufficient to determine the directional object of ⲉⲩϩⲉ†ⲉ ⲉ- 'they fall to'. Likely a single-letter article or preposition completion but unrecoverable.
11 chars with no traces; the prepositional phrase governing 'of the body' cannot be recovered.
5 chars; could be ⲁⲣⲭⲱⲛ 'archons' or another body-bearer term, but no constraining traces.
4 chars with partial 'ⲱⲛ'; could complete ⲁⲓⲱⲛ or ⲁⲣⲭⲱⲛ but the genitive chain is too uncertain.
10 chars with no traces; the clause introducing 'the lions' is unrecoverable.
2 chars; insufficient context to determine the connector after 'the lions'.
3 chars before ⲉⲧⲙ̄ⲙⲉⲩ ⲧⲉ ⲧϣⲁⲣⲡ 'is the first (fem.)'; demonstrative ⲧⲁⲓ̈ 'this (fem.)' agrees with feminine ⲧϣⲁⲣⲡ and matches the Kephalaia summary formula.

Direct parallel to §3761: ⲧⲱⲁⲣⲡ ⲓ̈ⲙⲙⲛⲧⲭⲁⲭⲉ ⲉⲧⲁⲥⲱⲱⲡⲉ ϩⲙ ⲡⲕⲉⲕⲉ 'the first Enmity which came to be in the Darkness' — the same formula closes here. The estimated 5 chars is exceeded but the formulaic identity is decisive.
Completes preposition ϩⲙ̄ 'in' before ⲡⲓ-.

7 chars containing partial 'ⲉϩⲁ'; ⲡⲉϩⲁⲉ 'the last' followed by genitive ⲛ̄ fits 'the last of the offspring of the prison, the mighty boundary' — coheres with the consummation register (panaretos / the bound self at the bolos in the lexicon).
Editor's restoration: ⲛ̄ⲣⲓⲅⲁⲥ = ⲡⲣⲓⲣⲁⲥ < Greek πέρας 'boundary'.
9 chars with single trace 'ⲣ'; the connective introducing 'those archons who…' is unrecoverable.
2 chars; demonstrative ⲛⲏ 'those (who)' before relative ⲉⲧⲟⲩⲱⲛϩ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ — 'those manifested'. Standard Lycopolitan distal demonstrative.
4 chars; the subject of ⲥⲉⲱⲭⲛⲉ ⲧⲏⲣⲟⲩ 'they all shall cease' is too damaged to recover.
3 chars; the temporal/manner phrase before ⲟⲩϩⲁⲉ 'a last' cannot be principled.
2 chars opening the clause; insufficient constraint.
2 chars; ϣⲟ 'thousand' is fixed by §3793 ⲟⲩⲓ̈ⲉⲣⲟ ⲅⲁⲣ ⲛ̄ⲟⲩⲱⲧ ϩⲛ̄ ϣⲟ ⲛ̄ⲗⲉⲣⲟ — 'one river out of a thousand rivers'. The construction 'the rivers being reckoned to a thousand' is the same image.
Final ϩ of ⲡⲕⲁϩ 'the earth' / 'the land' — the river of Judgment running upon the ground.
6 chars with partial 'ⲛⲧⲉ'; could be a genitive chain but the construction is unrecoverable.
Editor's restoration: ⲉⲧ-ⲙ̄ⲙⲉⲩ 'that one (there)' — standard distal demonstrative completing the exclamation about the great god.
7 chars with no traces; the predicate clause about the lions is unrecoverable.
Direct parallel to §3796: ⲡⲣⲱⲙⲉ ⲉⲧⲁϩⲣ̄ⲫⲟⲣⲉ 'the man who has worn'. Same construction here for the First Man who clothed himself in the elements — also matches the chapter title.
